newsitem.title: USA: Save energy with fluorescent bulbs, U.S. gov't says.
newsitem.headline: Save energy with fluorescent bulbs, U.S. gov't says.

text.p: Households could save one-third of the electricity they use for lighting if they replace their incandescent lightbulbs with compact fluorescent bulbs, the U.S. Energy Information Administration said Monday.
Using fluorescent lights instead of the inefficient incandescent lights could save homes almost 32 billion kilowatthours of electricity a year, EIA said.
But it added that the energy savings would take some time to translate into dollar savings because compact fluorescent bulbs cost more than twenty times more than standard bulbs.

In the New York City area, which has high electricity rates, homes would start saving money after two years, while in the Pacific Northwest, which has the lowest electricity rates, homes would start saving only after four years.
The average home uses 940 kilowatthours of electricity a year for $83 on average, according to EIA.
